scenes.title: A tiny sensor inside your device
The proof mass responds to motion
From microscopic motion to a step count

vo.text: Your phone or fitness band can count steps with a tiny chip called an accelerometer.
vo.speak: Your phone or fitness band can count steps with a tiny chip called an accelerometer.

vo.text: Inside this accelerometer, a microscopic proof mass shifts slightly when your body moves.
vo.speak: Inside this accelerometer, a microscopic proof mass shifts slightly when your body moves.

vo.text: Tiny flexible springs hold the mass inside the chip while allowing that small movement.
vo.speak: Tiny flexible springs hold the mass inside the chip while allowing that small movement.

vo.text: As the mass shifts, the spacing between interlocking capacitor fingers changes.
vo.speak: As the mass shifts, the spacing between interlocking capacitor fingers changes.

vo.text: The accelerometer's electronics convert that spacing change into an acceleration signal.
vo.speak: The accelerometer's electronics convert that spacing change into an acceleration signal.

vo.text: During walking, the signal contains a repeating pattern from each step and other body motion.
vo.speak: During walking, the signal contains a repeating pattern from each step and other body motion.

vo.text: Software filters noise and looks for the rhythm and strength of genuine steps, rather than counting every bump.
vo.speak: Software filters noise and looks for the rhythm and strength of genuine steps, rather than counting every bump.

vo.text: Each accepted step pattern advances the step counter by one.
vo.speak: Each accepted step pattern advances the step counter by one.

vo.text: So your step count begins with motion inside the accelerometer and ends with software recognizing a walking pattern.
vo.speak: So your step count begins with motion inside the accelerometer and ends with software recognizing a walking pattern.
